note: RAGE (https://darths-rage.netlify.app/) is capture-class: a single-file three.js action game served by Netlify at the origin root. §0.4 fork-over-mirror was checked on 2026-10-13 — no public upstream repo exists (the page carries no github/gitlab/bitbucket reference; a GitHub search finds only unrelated projects), so the mirror stands. Derived pipeline: capture → pinned prettier 3.9.6 (module API, default options, single pass verified idempotent — never the CLI: it respects .gitignore and can silently echo its input) → the entry document's inline <script> becomes readable/index-inline-1.pretty.js and its two inline <style> blocks become readable/index-inline-1|2.pretty.css (every pretty provably NOT byte-identical to its capture block; readable/index-inline-map.json records each block's exact byte range + sha256). Structure (2026-10-14 pass, evidence tools/probe-structure.mjs): 0 sourceMappingURL occurrences and 0 *.map files across the 72 captured files — no original tree can be reconstructed from maps; the inline script is one classic IIFE with 0 import/export occurrences and no factory family, so the real structure the bytes expose is the author's own 21 top-level section banners (`/* ===== level ===== */`, two-space indent). src/ slices are cut at those section boundaries (35 statement-aligned slice windows: sections longer than the 350-line cap split into -a/-b/... parts) and named after the sections (src/boot.js, src/level-a.js, src/updates-c.js, …). The IIFE wrapper head/tail and body statements that are not standalone at module top level (the engine guard, the renderer try guard and the sfx declaration each contain a top-level `return`) are skipped sections, indexed but never sliced. Every slice parses standalone under `node --input-type=module --check -` and round-trips byte-exact to its recorded readable line range (through the recorded rename map when rename-map.json carries one). Stylesheet rule — the two inline <style> blocks are wholeFile sections, never sliced. Non-code payloads (MP3 audio, WebP images, favicon.ico and the eight glTF model/geometry JSON payloads) are hashed notRendered records (bytes + sha256, no pretty pass). The CDN dependencies (nine jsdelivr three.js r147 scripts, the Google Fonts stylesheet) were never captured (socker precedent, PLAN §1) and have no derived layer; tools/capture.mjs --check lists them as external off-origin references. The semantic rename layer (tools/names.json → tools/apply-names.mjs, recovered into rename-map.json by tools/recover-scoped-map.mjs, re-applied on every re-cut) names the game's own opaque short bindings (byId, vec3, materials, level constants, scratch objects, audioEngine, …); the script is authored and already semantic, so only the genuinely opaque chunk-scope names are renamed and vendor/global identifiers (THREE.*) are never touched. `node tools/audit.js` is the gate. Capture bytes are untouched by everything above; re-cut with `node tools/derive.mjs` after any capture refresh.

renderOptions._default: prettier 3.9.6, module API, default options, single pass (re-format verified idempotent at derive time) — never the CLI: it respects .gitignore and can silently echo its input
renderOptions.json: parser json, no plugins (inline importmap blocks, if any)

structure.moduleBoundaries: none exposed — the inline script is one classic IIFE (`(() => { … })();`) with 0 import/export occurrences, no factory family and no export table (evidence: tools/probe-structure.mjs). The real structure the bytes declare is the author's 21 top-level section banners; slices are cut at them, and the parts of oversized sections (-a/-b/…) follow the desimayhem semantic-slice precedent.
structure.sourceMaps: none — 0 sourceMappingURL occurrences and 0 *.map files across the 72 captured files (scanned by tools/probe-structure.mjs), so the derivation stays a prettier/section-slice pass.
structure.sections: 21 banners → 22 sections (with the banner-less boot preamble) → 35 statement-aligned slice windows

source: readable/: 3 inline twin(s) (1 script → 35 section-aligned slices, 2 CSS pretties wholeFile); src/: 35 section-aligned slice(s) across 22 section(s); 5 skipped section(s); 2 wholeFile section(s); capture: 72 files under .upstream/manifest.json; inline scan: index.html (3 content block(s)); notRendered: 71 hashed payload record(s).

inline.note: the entry document carries one inline <script> (the whole game, 170,041 B) and two inline <style> blocks; every content block has a readable twin recorded in readable/index-inline-map.json with its exact byte range + sha256. The nine external <script src> loads (jsdelivr three.js r147) are CDN dependencies and are not derived.

rename.namesSource: tools/names.json (reviewed worklist) → tools/apply-names.mjs (scope-aware writer) → recovered by tools/recover-scoped-map.mjs
rename.note: Semantic renames are recorded per slice in rename-map.json and re-applied on every re-cut. The script is authored (not minified), so the campaign renames only the genuinely opaque chunk-scope names (short utility aliases, scratch vectors/quaternions, level-constant abbreviations); the rest keep the author's own names. THREE.* property names and all globals/vendor identifiers are never renamed.
